meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks whether external CDN scripts and stylesheets utilize Subresource Integrity (integrity and crossorigin attributes).
meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
meta.defaultFix: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

findings.name: ssl/tls check
findings.detail: TLSv1.3 | expires: Jan 21 15:06:20 2027 GMT

meta.title: SSL / TLS Certificate & Encryption
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies SSL certificate validity, expiration, hostname matching, and secure TLS protocol versions.
meta.whyItMatters: Expired or untrusted certificates cause browser warnings and leave traffic vulnerable to interception.
meta.defaultFix: Renew your SSL certificate, enable auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt, and disable obsolete TLS 1.0/1.1.

meta.title: Symfony Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Symfony WebProfiler toolbar (_profiler), debug routes, and config files.
meta.whyItMatters: Symfony WebProfiler exposes all request data, database credentials, and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure APP_ENV=prod and remove web-profiler-bundle from production environments.

meta.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if user inputs in query parameters are reflected unsanitized in the HTML page body.
meta.whyItMatters: XSS allows attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in victims' browsers, stealing cookies and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.

meta.title: Administrative Panels Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for publicly exposed administrative dashboards and login panels (e.g., /admin, /administrator, /cpanel).
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed admin interfaces attract automated brute-force attacks and credential stuffing.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict access by IP whitelist, VPN, or require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

meta.title: AI & LLM Endpoint Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for publicly exposed AI/LLM API routes (e.g., /api/chat, /api/generate, /v1/chat/completions) and vector DB endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected AI endpoints invite costly token theft, denial-of-wallet attacks, and prompt injection exploits.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.

meta.title: Sensitive API Endpoints
meta.plainExplanation: Discovers exposed internal API endpoints, debug endpoints, and Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
meta.whyItMatters: Publicly readable API endpoints can leak system architectures, internal schemas, and unprotected administrative actions.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication and role-based access control on all internal endpoints and disable debug routes in production.

findings.name: clickjacking protection

issues.issue: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible

findings.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

meta.title: Clickjacking Protection
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if your web pages can be embedded in an iframe on third-party websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can trick users into clicking invisible buttons or submitting forms on your site while thinking they are on another site.
meta.defaultFix: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.

meta.title: CodeIgniter Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for known CodeIgniter vulnerabilities, exposed writable logs, and system folders.
meta.whyItMatters: Outdated CodeIgniter versions and exposed application logs can lead to remote code execution and credential leakage.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade CodeIgniter to the latest release and ensure application/system folders are outside the web root.

findings.name: cookie security
findings.detail: No cookies set

meta.title: Cookie Security Attributes
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags configured.
meta.whyItMatters: Cookies missing HttpOnly can be stolen via XSS, and cookies missing Secure can be intercepted over unencrypted networks.
meta.defaultFix: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

findings.name: cors misconfiguration
findings.detail: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (wildcard)
findings.fix: Replace the wildcard '*' with a specific whitelist of trusted origins in your Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

meta.title: CORS Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies like wildcard origins with credentials.
meta.whyItMatters: Permissive CORS allows malicious third-party websites to read sensitive user data from your API via cross-origin requests.
meta.defaultFix: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

findings.name: php-cgi RCE (CVE-2024-4577)
findings.detail: No PHP-CGI binary found at common paths

meta.title: PHP CGI Argument Injection (CVE-2024-4577)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for critical Windows PHP CGI argument injection vulnerability allowing remote code execution.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can execute arbitrary command-line code on the server without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Update PHP to patched versions (8.3.8+, 8.2.20+, 8.1.29+) and rewrite URL query strings to disallow argument injection.

meta.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if web server directories without index files display automatic file listings.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to browse internal folder contents, discover forgotten backups, uploaded files, and source code.
meta.defaultFix: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

meta.title: Drupal CMS Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Drupal installations for end-of-life versions, exposed CHANGELOG files, and administrative routes.
meta.whyItMatters: Unsupported Drupal versions contain known critical vulnerabilities that can lead to complete site takeover.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade to an actively supported Drupal release and restrict access to CHANGELOG.txt and admin paths.

meta.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if environment configuration files (.env, .env.backup, etc.) are downloadable from the web.
meta.whyItMatters: .env files usually contain database passwords, API secrets, JWT keys, and payment gateway tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

meta.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed production JavaScript source maps (.js.map), debug modes, and hardcoded API tokens.
meta.whyItMatters: Source maps reconstruct original client-side source code, revealing internal endpoints, comments, and architectural flaws.
meta.defaultFix: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

meta.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the .git folder or .git/HEAD is publicly accessible on the web server.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Git folders allow attackers to download your entire source code repository, history, and embedded secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

meta.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if GraphQL schema introspection is enabled in production environments.
meta.whyItMatters: Introspection exposes your entire GraphQL schema, types, queries, and mutations to any unauthenticated caller.
meta.defaultFix: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

meta.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether dangerous or unnecessary HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE, OPTIONS) are accepted.
meta.whyItMatters: TRACE enables Cross-Site Tracing (XST) attacks; improperly configured PUT/DELETE allows unauthorized file modification.
meta.defaultFix: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

findings.name: https redirect
findings.detail: HTTP → HTTPS redirect in place (301 permanent)

meta.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirection
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that unencrypted HTTP connections are automatically redirected to secure HTTPS.
meta.whyItMatters: Unencrypted HTTP traffic can be intercepted, read, or modified by attackers on public networks.
meta.defaultFix: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

meta.title: Laravel Ignition Debug RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Detects exposed Laravel Ignition error page endpoints susceptible to known remote code execution exploits.
meta.whyItMatters: Ignition debug routes in production can allow an attacker to run arbitrary PHP code on the server.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in production and ensure ignition package is only in require-dev.

findings.name: jwt security
findings.detail: No JWT tokens found in probed endpoints

meta.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits JWT implementations for "none" algorithm flaws, weak secret keys, and exposed token endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Vulnerable JWT implementations allow attackers to forge tokens and impersonate administrators.
meta.defaultFix: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

meta.title: Laravel Auth Routes & CSRF
meta.plainExplanation: Checks Laravel login, registration, and password reset endpoints for missing CSRF protection and brute-force defenses.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected authentication routes enable credential brute-forcing and cross-site request forgery.
meta.defaultFix: Enable RateLimiter on authentication routes and ensure VerifyCsrfToken middleware is active.

meta.title: Laravel Debug Mode Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel debug mode (APP_DEBUG=true) is accidentally enabled in production.
meta.whyItMatters: Debug mode displays detailed stack traces, database queries, and environment secrets when errors occur.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in your production .env file.

findings.name: laravel env manipulation (CVE-2024-52301)
findings.detail: No environment manipulation detected — likely patched or register_argc_argv disabled

meta.title: Laravel Environment Manipulation
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for parameter injection vulnerability attempting to switch application environment to local or debug.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to manipulate framework runtime behavior and trigger verbose error responses.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure framework dependencies are up-to-date and disallow CLI argument reflection in HTTP contexts.

meta.title: Laravel Livewire Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Livewire endpoints (/livewire/update, /livewire/upload-file) for authorization bypasses and missing validation.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Livewire component endpoints can allow unauthorized state modification or file upload vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure all Livewire components enforce authorization checks inside render/mount and validate all component properties.

meta.title: Laravel Storage & Log Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel storage/logs, framework caches, or session files are accessible over HTTP.
meta.whyItMatters: Storage logs contain user data, API errors, session identifiers, and sensitive system details.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure only the "public" directory is served as the web root, not the project root directory.

meta.title: Laravel Telescope Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel Telescope debugging dashboard (/telescope) is publicly accessible.
meta.whyItMatters: Telescope records all requests, SQL queries, mail messages, and user sessions in real-time.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Telescope access with Telescope::auth gate or disable it completely in production.

meta.title: Magento / Adobe Commerce Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible Magento admin URLs, downloader tools, and config files like local.xml.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed local.xml files leak database credentials and encryption keys for customer passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Block web access to /app, /downloader, and /var directories in web server configuration.

meta.title: Magento CosmicSting (CVE-2024-34102)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server, including secret encryption keys.
meta.defaultFix: Apply Adobe security patch APSB24-40 immediately or upgrade Magento to 2.4.7-p1+.

meta.title: Next.js & React Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Next.js applications for Server Actions exposures, source maps, SSR data leaks, and dev headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Next.js Server Actions can inadvertently expose internal server functions, while hydration state may leak sensitive user secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication in Server Actions, omit source maps in production, and never expose server secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars.

meta.title: Node.js & Express Security
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed package.json, node_modules directories, and X-Powered-By: Express headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed package.json reveals exact dependency versions, making it easy for attackers to target known CVEs.
meta.defaultFix: Remove X-Powered-By with app.disable("x-powered-by") and ensure node_modules is outside web root.

meta.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if redirect parameters (e.g. ?url=, ?redirect=) accept arbitrary external websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers craft believable phishing links using your trusted domain that redirect victims to malicious sites.
meta.defaultFix: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.

meta.title: PHP Backup & Old Files
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for forgotten backup files such as index.php.bak, config.php.old, or index.php~.
meta.whyItMatters: Web servers often do not execute PHP for .bak or .old extensions, dumping raw PHP source code and credentials.
meta.defaultFix: Never store backup or temporary files inside the web server document root; delete backup files after deployment.

meta.title: PHP-FPM & CGI Status Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible /fpm-ping, /php-status, or cgi-bin PHP binaries.
meta.whyItMatters: FPM status pages leak active client IPs, query strings, and script paths; exposed CGI binaries allow command execution.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict /status and /ping endpoints in Nginx/Apache to localhost (127.0.0.1) only.

meta.title: Insecure PHP Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for unsafe PHP directives such as allow_url_include, display_errors, or register_globals.
meta.whyItMatters: Insecure PHP configurations enable Remote File Inclusion (RFI) and information disclosure.
meta.defaultFix: Turn off display_errors, disable allow_url_include, and harden php.ini.

meta.title: PHP Error & Exception Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the web server displays verbose PHP warning, notice, or fatal error messages.
meta.whyItMatters: Error messages display filesystem paths, line numbers, and database query structures to visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Set display_errors = Off and log_errors = On in php.ini.

meta.title: PHPInfo Page Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for public phpinfo.php, info.php, or test.php files.
meta.whyItMatters: phpinfo() outputs complete server environment variables, PHP modules, OS versions, and database usernames.
meta.defaultFix: Delete any phpinfo() script files from public production servers.

meta.title: PHP Local File Inclusion (LFI)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

findings.name: php version (eol)
findings.detail: PHP version not disclosed in headers

meta.title: PHP Version Disclosure & EOL
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if PHP version is disclosed via X-Powered-By headers and whether that version is end-of-life.
meta.whyItMatters: EOL versions no longer receive security fixes; disclosing the exact version makes targeting known exploits trivial.
meta.defaultFix: Set expose_php = Off in php.ini and upgrade PHP to an actively supported version (8.2+).

meta.title: PHPUnit Eval-Stdin RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed /vendor/phpunit/.../eval-stdin.php test runner endpoint (CVE-2017-9841).
meta.whyItMatters: This endpoint executes arbitrary PHP code sent via POST without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Remove the /vendor directory from public web access and install test dependencies with --no-dev in production.

meta.title: Python (Django & Flask) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed requirements.txt, Django debug mode, and Werkzeug/Flask interactive debugger.
meta.whyItMatters: Werkzeug interactive debugger allows unauthenticated remote code execution via interactive console.
meta.defaultFix: Set DEBUG = False in Django and disable debug mode in Flask before deploying to production.

findings.name: rate limiting
findings.detail: 15/15 burst requests succeeded — no rate limiting detected (brute-force risk)
findings.fix: Implement rate limiting at the application level (e.g., Laravel's ThrottleRequests) or web server level (e.g., Nginx 'limit_req') to protect against brute-force and DoS attacks.

meta.title: Rate Limiting & Abuse Prevention
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether rapid bursts of requests trigger HTTP 429 Too Many Requests or rate-limit headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Endpoints without rate limiting are vulnerable to denial of service, credential stuffing, and scraping.
meta.defaultFix: Implement rate limiting at the reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx limit_req) or application layer.

meta.title: Robots.txt & Sitemap Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Analyzes robots.txt and sitemap.xml for disallow rules pointing to sensitive hidden directories.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers read robots.txt to discover hidden admin panels, staging areas, and private endpoints.
meta.defaultFix: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.

findings.name: security headers
findings.fix: Implement the missing security headers in your web server configuration (e.g., in Nginx 'add_header' or Apache 'Header set') to protect against XSS, clickjacking, and mime-type sniffing.

meta.title: HTTP Security Headers
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical defensive headers: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.
meta.whyItMatters: Missing security headers leaves users exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and cross-site scripting.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to supply HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Referrer-Policy headers.

meta.title: Sensitive Files & Configurations
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed database dumps, configuration backups, credentials, and docker-compose files.
meta.whyItMatters: Leaked configuration and database dump files grant instant access to sensitive databases.
meta.defaultFix: Store backups, SQL dumps, and configuration files outside the web root directory.

meta.title: Server Software Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Server header reveals software names and exact version numbers (e.g., Apache/2.4.41).
meta.whyItMatters: Detailed version information allows attackers to look up specific CVE exploits for that exact version.
meta.defaultFix: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.

meta.title: Spring Boot Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Spring Boot Actuator endpoints (/actuator, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump) and Whitelabel error pages.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Actuator endpoints can leak environment variables, database credentials, and heap dumps containing cleartext passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Actuator endpoints using Spring Security or set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info.

meta.title: Database Error Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if query strings trigger verbose database error messages (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL).
meta.whyItMatters: Database error messages reveal schema structures and confirm the presence of SQL injection vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

meta.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests input fields and parameters for SQL syntax manipulation and time-based delays.
meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks whether external CDN scripts and stylesheets utilize Subresource Integrity (integrity and crossorigin attributes).
meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
meta.defaultFix: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected authentication routes enable credential brute-forcing and cross-site request forgery.
meta.defaultFix: Enable RateLimiter on authentication routes and ensure VerifyCsrfToken middleware is active.

meta.title: Laravel Debug Mode Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel debug mode (APP_DEBUG=true) is accidentally enabled in production.
meta.whyItMatters: Debug mode displays detailed stack traces, database queries, and environment secrets when errors occur.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in your production .env file.

findings.name: laravel env manipulation (CVE-2024-52301)
findings.detail: No environment manipulation detected — likely patched or register_argc_argv disabled

meta.title: Laravel Environment Manipulation
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for parameter injection vulnerability attempting to switch application environment to local or debug.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to manipulate framework runtime behavior and trigger verbose error responses.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure framework dependencies are up-to-date and disallow CLI argument reflection in HTTP contexts.

meta.title: Laravel Livewire Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Livewire endpoints (/livewire/update, /livewire/upload-file) for authorization bypasses and missing validation.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Livewire component endpoints can allow unauthorized state modification or file upload vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure all Livewire components enforce authorization checks inside render/mount and validate all component properties.

meta.title: Laravel Storage & Log Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel storage/logs, framework caches, or session files are accessible over HTTP.
meta.whyItMatters: Storage logs contain user data, API errors, session identifiers, and sensitive system details.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure only the "public" directory is served as the web root, not the project root directory.

meta.title: Laravel Telescope Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel Telescope debugging dashboard (/telescope) is publicly accessible.
meta.whyItMatters: Telescope records all requests, SQL queries, mail messages, and user sessions in real-time.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Telescope access with Telescope::auth gate or disable it completely in production.

meta.title: Magento / Adobe Commerce Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible Magento admin URLs, downloader tools, and config files like local.xml.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed local.xml files leak database credentials and encryption keys for customer passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Block web access to /app, /downloader, and /var directories in web server configuration.

meta.title: Magento CosmicSting (CVE-2024-34102)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server, including secret encryption keys.
meta.defaultFix: Apply Adobe security patch APSB24-40 immediately or upgrade Magento to 2.4.7-p1+.

meta.title: Next.js & React Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Next.js applications for Server Actions exposures, source maps, SSR data leaks, and dev headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Next.js Server Actions can inadvertently expose internal server functions, while hydration state may leak sensitive user secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication in Server Actions, omit source maps in production, and never expose server secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars.

meta.title: Node.js & Express Security
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed package.json, node_modules directories, and X-Powered-By: Express headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed package.json reveals exact dependency versions, making it easy for attackers to target known CVEs.
meta.defaultFix: Remove X-Powered-By with app.disable("x-powered-by") and ensure node_modules is outside web root.

meta.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if redirect parameters (e.g. ?url=, ?redirect=) accept arbitrary external websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers craft believable phishing links using your trusted domain that redirect victims to malicious sites.
meta.defaultFix: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.

meta.title: PHP Backup & Old Files
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for forgotten backup files such as index.php.bak, config.php.old, or index.php~.
meta.whyItMatters: Web servers often do not execute PHP for .bak or .old extensions, dumping raw PHP source code and credentials.
meta.defaultFix: Never store backup or temporary files inside the web server document root; delete backup files after deployment.

meta.title: PHP-FPM & CGI Status Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible /fpm-ping, /php-status, or cgi-bin PHP binaries.
meta.whyItMatters: FPM status pages leak active client IPs, query strings, and script paths; exposed CGI binaries allow command execution.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict /status and /ping endpoints in Nginx/Apache to localhost (127.0.0.1) only.

meta.title: Insecure PHP Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for unsafe PHP directives such as allow_url_include, display_errors, or register_globals.
meta.whyItMatters: Insecure PHP configurations enable Remote File Inclusion (RFI) and information disclosure.
meta.defaultFix: Turn off display_errors, disable allow_url_include, and harden php.ini.

meta.title: PHP Error & Exception Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the web server displays verbose PHP warning, notice, or fatal error messages.
meta.whyItMatters: Error messages display filesystem paths, line numbers, and database query structures to visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Set display_errors = Off and log_errors = On in php.ini.

meta.title: PHPInfo Page Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for public phpinfo.php, info.php, or test.php files.
meta.whyItMatters: phpinfo() outputs complete server environment variables, PHP modules, OS versions, and database usernames.
meta.defaultFix: Delete any phpinfo() script files from public production servers.

meta.title: PHP Local File Inclusion (LFI)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

findings.name: php version (eol)
findings.detail: PHP version not disclosed in headers

meta.title: PHP Version Disclosure & EOL
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if PHP version is disclosed via X-Powered-By headers and whether that version is end-of-life.
meta.whyItMatters: EOL versions no longer receive security fixes; disclosing the exact version makes targeting known exploits trivial.
meta.defaultFix: Set expose_php = Off in php.ini and upgrade PHP to an actively supported version (8.2+).

meta.title: PHPUnit Eval-Stdin RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed /vendor/phpunit/.../eval-stdin.php test runner endpoint (CVE-2017-9841).
meta.whyItMatters: This endpoint executes arbitrary PHP code sent via POST without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Remove the /vendor directory from public web access and install test dependencies with --no-dev in production.

meta.title: Python (Django & Flask) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed requirements.txt, Django debug mode, and Werkzeug/Flask interactive debugger.
meta.whyItMatters: Werkzeug interactive debugger allows unauthenticated remote code execution via interactive console.
meta.defaultFix: Set DEBUG = False in Django and disable debug mode in Flask before deploying to production.

findings.name: rate limiting
findings.detail: 15/15 burst requests succeeded — no rate limiting detected (brute-force risk)
findings.fix: Implement rate limiting at the application level (e.g., Laravel's ThrottleRequests) or web server level (e.g., Nginx 'limit_req') to protect against brute-force and DoS attacks.

meta.title: Rate Limiting & Abuse Prevention
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether rapid bursts of requests trigger HTTP 429 Too Many Requests or rate-limit headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Endpoints without rate limiting are vulnerable to denial of service, credential stuffing, and scraping.
meta.defaultFix: Implement rate limiting at the reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx limit_req) or application layer.

meta.title: Robots.txt & Sitemap Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Analyzes robots.txt and sitemap.xml for disallow rules pointing to sensitive hidden directories.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers read robots.txt to discover hidden admin panels, staging areas, and private endpoints.
meta.defaultFix: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.

findings.name: security headers
findings.fix: Implement the missing security headers in your web server configuration (e.g., in Nginx 'add_header' or Apache 'Header set') to protect against XSS, clickjacking, and mime-type sniffing.

meta.title: HTTP Security Headers
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical defensive headers: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.
meta.whyItMatters: Missing security headers leaves users exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and cross-site scripting.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to supply HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Referrer-Policy headers.

meta.title: Sensitive Files & Configurations
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed database dumps, configuration backups, credentials, and docker-compose files.
meta.whyItMatters: Leaked configuration and database dump files grant instant access to sensitive databases.
meta.defaultFix: Store backups, SQL dumps, and configuration files outside the web root directory.

meta.title: Server Software Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Server header reveals software names and exact version numbers (e.g., Apache/2.4.41).
meta.whyItMatters: Detailed version information allows attackers to look up specific CVE exploits for that exact version.
meta.defaultFix: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.

meta.title: Spring Boot Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Spring Boot Actuator endpoints (/actuator, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump) and Whitelabel error pages.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Actuator endpoints can leak environment variables, database credentials, and heap dumps containing cleartext passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Actuator endpoints using Spring Security or set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info.

meta.title: Database Error Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if query strings trigger verbose database error messages (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL).
meta.whyItMatters: Database error messages reveal schema structures and confirm the presence of SQL injection vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

meta.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests input fields and parameters for SQL syntax manipulation and time-based delays.
meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks whether external CDN scripts and stylesheets utilize Subresource Integrity (integrity and crossorigin attributes).
meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
meta.defaultFix: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

findings.name: ssl/tls check
findings.detail: TLSv1.3 | expires: Jan 21 15:06:20 2027 GMT

meta.title: SSL / TLS Certificate & Encryption
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies SSL certificate validity, expiration, hostname matching, and secure TLS protocol versions.
meta.whyItMatters: Expired or untrusted certificates cause browser warnings and leave traffic vulnerable to interception.
meta.defaultFix: Renew your SSL certificate, enable auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt, and disable obsolete TLS 1.0/1.1.

meta.title: Symfony Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Symfony WebProfiler toolbar (_profiler), debug routes, and config files.
meta.whyItMatters: Symfony WebProfiler exposes all request data, database credentials, and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure APP_ENV=prod and remove web-profiler-bundle from production environments.

meta.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if user inputs in query parameters are reflected unsanitized in the HTML page body.
meta.whyItMatters: XSS allows attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in victims' browsers, stealing cookies and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.

meta.title: Administrative Panels Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for publicly exposed administrative dashboards and login panels (e.g., /admin, /administrator, /cpanel).
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed admin interfaces attract automated brute-force attacks and credential stuffing.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict access by IP whitelist, VPN, or require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

meta.title: AI & LLM Endpoint Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for publicly exposed AI/LLM API routes (e.g., /api/chat, /api/generate, /v1/chat/completions) and vector DB endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected AI endpoints invite costly token theft, denial-of-wallet attacks, and prompt injection exploits.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.

meta.title: Sensitive API Endpoints
meta.plainExplanation: Discovers exposed internal API endpoints, debug endpoints, and Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
meta.whyItMatters: Publicly readable API endpoints can leak system architectures, internal schemas, and unprotected administrative actions.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication and role-based access control on all internal endpoints and disable debug routes in production.

findings.name: clickjacking protection

issues.issue: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible

findings.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

meta.title: Clickjacking Protection
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if your web pages can be embedded in an iframe on third-party websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can trick users into clicking invisible buttons or submitting forms on your site while thinking they are on another site.
meta.defaultFix: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.

meta.title: CodeIgniter Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for known CodeIgniter vulnerabilities, exposed writable logs, and system folders.
meta.whyItMatters: Outdated CodeIgniter versions and exposed application logs can lead to remote code execution and credential leakage.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade CodeIgniter to the latest release and ensure application/system folders are outside the web root.

findings.name: cookie security
findings.detail: No cookies set

meta.title: Cookie Security Attributes
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags configured.
meta.whyItMatters: Cookies missing HttpOnly can be stolen via XSS, and cookies missing Secure can be intercepted over unencrypted networks.
meta.defaultFix: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

findings.name: cors misconfiguration
findings.detail: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (wildcard)
findings.fix: Replace the wildcard '*' with a specific whitelist of trusted origins in your Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

meta.title: CORS Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies like wildcard origins with credentials.
meta.whyItMatters: Permissive CORS allows malicious third-party websites to read sensitive user data from your API via cross-origin requests.
meta.defaultFix: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

findings.name: php-cgi RCE (CVE-2024-4577)
findings.detail: No PHP-CGI binary found at common paths

meta.title: PHP CGI Argument Injection (CVE-2024-4577)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for critical Windows PHP CGI argument injection vulnerability allowing remote code execution.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can execute arbitrary command-line code on the server without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Update PHP to patched versions (8.3.8+, 8.2.20+, 8.1.29+) and rewrite URL query strings to disallow argument injection.

meta.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if web server directories without index files display automatic file listings.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to browse internal folder contents, discover forgotten backups, uploaded files, and source code.
meta.defaultFix: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

meta.title: Drupal CMS Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Drupal installations for end-of-life versions, exposed CHANGELOG files, and administrative routes.
meta.whyItMatters: Unsupported Drupal versions contain known critical vulnerabilities that can lead to complete site takeover.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade to an actively supported Drupal release and restrict access to CHANGELOG.txt and admin paths.

meta.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if environment configuration files (.env, .env.backup, etc.) are downloadable from the web.
meta.whyItMatters: .env files usually contain database passwords, API secrets, JWT keys, and payment gateway tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

meta.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed production JavaScript source maps (.js.map), debug modes, and hardcoded API tokens.
meta.whyItMatters: Source maps reconstruct original client-side source code, revealing internal endpoints, comments, and architectural flaws.
meta.defaultFix: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

meta.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the .git folder or .git/HEAD is publicly accessible on the web server.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Git folders allow attackers to download your entire source code repository, history, and embedded secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

meta.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if GraphQL schema introspection is enabled in production environments.
meta.whyItMatters: Introspection exposes your entire GraphQL schema, types, queries, and mutations to any unauthenticated caller.
meta.defaultFix: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

meta.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether dangerous or unnecessary HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE, OPTIONS) are accepted.
meta.whyItMatters: TRACE enables Cross-Site Tracing (XST) attacks; improperly configured PUT/DELETE allows unauthorized file modification.
meta.defaultFix: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

findings.name: https redirect
findings.detail: HTTP → HTTPS redirect in place (301 permanent)

meta.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirection
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that unencrypted HTTP connections are automatically redirected to secure HTTPS.
meta.whyItMatters: Unencrypted HTTP traffic can be intercepted, read, or modified by attackers on public networks.
meta.defaultFix: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

meta.title: Laravel Ignition Debug RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Detects exposed Laravel Ignition error page endpoints susceptible to known remote code execution exploits.
meta.whyItMatters: Ignition debug routes in production can allow an attacker to run arbitrary PHP code on the server.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in production and ensure ignition package is only in require-dev.

findings.name: jwt security
findings.detail: No JWT tokens found in probed endpoints

meta.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits JWT implementations for "none" algorithm flaws, weak secret keys, and exposed token endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Vulnerable JWT implementations allow attackers to forge tokens and impersonate administrators.
meta.defaultFix: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

meta.title: Laravel Auth Routes & CSRF
meta.plainExplanation: Checks Laravel login, registration, and password reset endpoints for missing CSRF protection and brute-force defenses.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected authentication routes enable credential brute-forcing and cross-site request forgery.
meta.defaultFix: Enable RateLimiter on authentication routes and ensure VerifyCsrfToken middleware is active.

meta.title: Laravel Debug Mode Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel debug mode (APP_DEBUG=true) is accidentally enabled in production.
meta.whyItMatters: Debug mode displays detailed stack traces, database queries, and environment secrets when errors occur.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in your production .env file.

meta.title: Spring Boot Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Spring Boot Actuator endpoints (/actuator, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump) and Whitelabel error pages.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Actuator endpoints can leak environment variables, database credentials, and heap dumps containing cleartext passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Actuator endpoints using Spring Security or set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info.

meta.title: Database Error Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if query strings trigger verbose database error messages (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL).
meta.whyItMatters: Database error messages reveal schema structures and confirm the presence of SQL injection vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

meta.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests input fields and parameters for SQL syntax manipulation and time-based delays.
meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.title: Supply Chain & Subresource Integrity (SRI)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks whether external CDN scripts and stylesheets utilize Subresource Integrity (integrity and crossorigin attributes).
meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
meta.defaultFix: Include cryptographic integrity hashes (e.g., integrity="sha384-...") on all external script and link tags.

findings.name: ssl/tls check
findings.detail: TLSv1.3 | expires: Jan 21 15:06:20 2027 GMT

meta.title: SSL / TLS Certificate & Encryption
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies SSL certificate validity, expiration, hostname matching, and secure TLS protocol versions.
meta.whyItMatters: Expired or untrusted certificates cause browser warnings and leave traffic vulnerable to interception.
meta.defaultFix: Renew your SSL certificate, enable auto-renewal via Let's Encrypt, and disable obsolete TLS 1.0/1.1.

meta.title: Symfony Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Symfony WebProfiler toolbar (_profiler), debug routes, and config files.
meta.whyItMatters: Symfony WebProfiler exposes all request data, database credentials, and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure APP_ENV=prod and remove web-profiler-bundle from production environments.

meta.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if user inputs in query parameters are reflected unsanitized in the HTML page body.
meta.whyItMatters: XSS allows attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in victims' browsers, stealing cookies and session tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.

meta.title: Administrative Panels Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for publicly exposed administrative dashboards and login panels (e.g., /admin, /administrator, /cpanel).
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed admin interfaces attract automated brute-force attacks and credential stuffing.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict access by IP whitelist, VPN, or require multi-factor authentication (MFA).

meta.title: AI & LLM Endpoint Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for publicly exposed AI/LLM API routes (e.g., /api/chat, /api/generate, /v1/chat/completions) and vector DB endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected AI endpoints invite costly token theft, denial-of-wallet attacks, and prompt injection exploits.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce strict authentication, user-level rate limiting, and input validation on all AI endpoints.

meta.title: Sensitive API Endpoints
meta.plainExplanation: Discovers exposed internal API endpoints, debug endpoints, and Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
meta.whyItMatters: Publicly readable API endpoints can leak system architectures, internal schemas, and unprotected administrative actions.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication and role-based access control on all internal endpoints and disable debug routes in production.

findings.name: clickjacking protection

issues.issue: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors — iframe embedding possible

findings.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or SAMEORIGIN) and 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none' (or 'self') headers to prevent unauthorized embedding in iframes.

meta.title: Clickjacking Protection
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if your web pages can be embedded in an iframe on third-party websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can trick users into clicking invisible buttons or submitting forms on your site while thinking they are on another site.
meta.defaultFix: Add the "X-Frame-Options: DENY" or "Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'" HTTP header.

meta.title: CodeIgniter Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for known CodeIgniter vulnerabilities, exposed writable logs, and system folders.
meta.whyItMatters: Outdated CodeIgniter versions and exposed application logs can lead to remote code execution and credential leakage.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade CodeIgniter to the latest release and ensure application/system folders are outside the web root.

findings.name: cookie security
findings.detail: No cookies set

meta.title: Cookie Security Attributes
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags configured.
meta.whyItMatters: Cookies missing HttpOnly can be stolen via XSS, and cookies missing Secure can be intercepted over unencrypted networks.
meta.defaultFix: Set "Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax" (or SameSite=Strict) on all session and sensitive cookies.

findings.name: cors misconfiguration
findings.detail: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (wildcard)
findings.fix: Replace the wildcard '*' with a specific whitelist of trusted origins in your Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

meta.title: CORS Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policies like wildcard origins with credentials.
meta.whyItMatters: Permissive CORS allows malicious third-party websites to read sensitive user data from your API via cross-origin requests.
meta.defaultFix: Specify explicit trusted origins in the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header and avoid reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials.

findings.name: php-cgi RCE (CVE-2024-4577)
findings.detail: No PHP-CGI binary found at common paths

meta.title: PHP CGI Argument Injection (CVE-2024-4577)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for critical Windows PHP CGI argument injection vulnerability allowing remote code execution.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers can execute arbitrary command-line code on the server without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Update PHP to patched versions (8.3.8+, 8.2.20+, 8.1.29+) and rewrite URL query strings to disallow argument injection.

meta.title: Directory Indexing / Listing
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if web server directories without index files display automatic file listings.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to browse internal folder contents, discover forgotten backups, uploaded files, and source code.
meta.defaultFix: Disable directory browsing in web server configuration (e.g., "Options -Indexes" in Apache, "autoindex off" in Nginx).

meta.title: Drupal CMS Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Drupal installations for end-of-life versions, exposed CHANGELOG files, and administrative routes.
meta.whyItMatters: Unsupported Drupal versions contain known critical vulnerabilities that can lead to complete site takeover.
meta.defaultFix: Upgrade to an actively supported Drupal release and restrict access to CHANGELOG.txt and admin paths.

meta.title: Environment File Exposure (.env)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if environment configuration files (.env, .env.backup, etc.) are downloadable from the web.
meta.whyItMatters: .env files usually contain database passwords, API secrets, JWT keys, and payment gateway tokens.
meta.defaultFix: Block web server access to all dotfiles (e.g. location ~ /\. { deny all; }) and store sensitive configs outside web roots.

meta.title: Frontend Source Maps & Dev Artifacts
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed production JavaScript source maps (.js.map), debug modes, and hardcoded API tokens.
meta.whyItMatters: Source maps reconstruct original client-side source code, revealing internal endpoints, comments, and architectural flaws.
meta.defaultFix: Do not deploy .map files to public production servers; generate source maps only for internal error tracking.

meta.title: Git Repository Exposure (.git)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the .git folder or .git/HEAD is publicly accessible on the web server.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Git folders allow attackers to download your entire source code repository, history, and embedded secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to strictly block access to the .git directory or exclude .git during deployment.

meta.title: GraphQL Introspection & Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if GraphQL schema introspection is enabled in production environments.
meta.whyItMatters: Introspection exposes your entire GraphQL schema, types, queries, and mutations to any unauthenticated caller.
meta.defaultFix: Disable GraphQL schema introspection in production deployments.

meta.title: Dangerous HTTP Methods
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether dangerous or unnecessary HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE, OPTIONS) are accepted.
meta.whyItMatters: TRACE enables Cross-Site Tracing (XST) attacks; improperly configured PUT/DELETE allows unauthorized file modification.
meta.defaultFix: Disable TRACE and restrict HTTP methods to only GET, POST, and HEAD for public web pages.

findings.name: https redirect
findings.detail: HTTP → HTTPS redirect in place (301 permanent)

meta.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirection
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies that unencrypted HTTP connections are automatically redirected to secure HTTPS.
meta.whyItMatters: Unencrypted HTTP traffic can be intercepted, read, or modified by attackers on public networks.
meta.defaultFix: Configure a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS across all web server hosts.

meta.title: Laravel Ignition Debug RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Detects exposed Laravel Ignition error page endpoints susceptible to known remote code execution exploits.
meta.whyItMatters: Ignition debug routes in production can allow an attacker to run arbitrary PHP code on the server.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in production and ensure ignition package is only in require-dev.

findings.name: jwt security
findings.detail: No JWT tokens found in probed endpoints

meta.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits JWT implementations for "none" algorithm flaws, weak secret keys, and exposed token endpoints.
meta.whyItMatters: Vulnerable JWT implementations allow attackers to forge tokens and impersonate administrators.
meta.defaultFix: Use strong cryptographic algorithms (RS256 or high-entropy HS256) and strictly reject tokens with "alg": "none".

meta.title: Laravel Auth Routes & CSRF
meta.plainExplanation: Checks Laravel login, registration, and password reset endpoints for missing CSRF protection and brute-force defenses.
meta.whyItMatters: Unprotected authentication routes enable credential brute-forcing and cross-site request forgery.
meta.defaultFix: Enable RateLimiter on authentication routes and ensure VerifyCsrfToken middleware is active.

meta.title: Laravel Debug Mode Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel debug mode (APP_DEBUG=true) is accidentally enabled in production.
meta.whyItMatters: Debug mode displays detailed stack traces, database queries, and environment secrets when errors occur.
meta.defaultFix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in your production .env file.

findings.name: laravel env manipulation (CVE-2024-52301)
findings.detail: No environment manipulation detected — likely patched or register_argc_argv disabled

meta.title: Laravel Environment Manipulation
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for parameter injection vulnerability attempting to switch application environment to local or debug.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows attackers to manipulate framework runtime behavior and trigger verbose error responses.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure framework dependencies are up-to-date and disallow CLI argument reflection in HTTP contexts.

meta.title: Laravel Livewire Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Livewire endpoints (/livewire/update, /livewire/upload-file) for authorization bypasses and missing validation.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Livewire component endpoints can allow unauthorized state modification or file upload vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure all Livewire components enforce authorization checks inside render/mount and validate all component properties.

meta.title: Laravel Storage & Log Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel storage/logs, framework caches, or session files are accessible over HTTP.
meta.whyItMatters: Storage logs contain user data, API errors, session identifiers, and sensitive system details.
meta.defaultFix: Ensure only the "public" directory is served as the web root, not the project root directory.

meta.title: Laravel Telescope Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Laravel Telescope debugging dashboard (/telescope) is publicly accessible.
meta.whyItMatters: Telescope records all requests, SQL queries, mail messages, and user sessions in real-time.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Telescope access with Telescope::auth gate or disable it completely in production.

meta.title: Magento / Adobe Commerce Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible Magento admin URLs, downloader tools, and config files like local.xml.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed local.xml files leak database credentials and encryption keys for customer passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Block web access to /app, /downloader, and /var directories in web server configuration.

meta.title: Magento CosmicSting (CVE-2024-34102)
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento.
meta.whyItMatters: Allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server, including secret encryption keys.
meta.defaultFix: Apply Adobe security patch APSB24-40 immediately or upgrade Magento to 2.4.7-p1+.

meta.title: Next.js & React Security
meta.plainExplanation: Audits Next.js applications for Server Actions exposures, source maps, SSR data leaks, and dev headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Next.js Server Actions can inadvertently expose internal server functions, while hydration state may leak sensitive user secrets.
meta.defaultFix: Enforce authentication in Server Actions, omit source maps in production, and never expose server secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars.

meta.title: Node.js & Express Security
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed package.json, node_modules directories, and X-Powered-By: Express headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed package.json reveals exact dependency versions, making it easy for attackers to target known CVEs.
meta.defaultFix: Remove X-Powered-By with app.disable("x-powered-by") and ensure node_modules is outside web root.

meta.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability
meta.plainExplanation: Tests if redirect parameters (e.g. ?url=, ?redirect=) accept arbitrary external websites.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers craft believable phishing links using your trusted domain that redirect victims to malicious sites.
meta.defaultFix: Validate target URLs against a strict whitelist of internal relative paths or approved domains.

meta.title: PHP Backup & Old Files
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for forgotten backup files such as index.php.bak, config.php.old, or index.php~.
meta.whyItMatters: Web servers often do not execute PHP for .bak or .old extensions, dumping raw PHP source code and credentials.
meta.defaultFix: Never store backup or temporary files inside the web server document root; delete backup files after deployment.

meta.title: PHP-FPM & CGI Status Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for accessible /fpm-ping, /php-status, or cgi-bin PHP binaries.
meta.whyItMatters: FPM status pages leak active client IPs, query strings, and script paths; exposed CGI binaries allow command execution.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict /status and /ping endpoints in Nginx/Apache to localhost (127.0.0.1) only.

meta.title: Insecure PHP Configuration
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for unsafe PHP directives such as allow_url_include, display_errors, or register_globals.
meta.whyItMatters: Insecure PHP configurations enable Remote File Inclusion (RFI) and information disclosure.
meta.defaultFix: Turn off display_errors, disable allow_url_include, and harden php.ini.

meta.title: PHP Error & Exception Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if the web server displays verbose PHP warning, notice, or fatal error messages.
meta.whyItMatters: Error messages display filesystem paths, line numbers, and database query structures to visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Set display_errors = Off and log_errors = On in php.ini.

meta.title: PHPInfo Page Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for public phpinfo.php, info.php, or test.php files.
meta.whyItMatters: phpinfo() outputs complete server environment variables, PHP modules, OS versions, and database usernames.
meta.defaultFix: Delete any phpinfo() script files from public production servers.

meta.title: PHP Local File Inclusion (LFI)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests for directory traversal vulnerabilities in file inclusion parameters (e.g. ?page=../../etc/passwd).
meta.whyItMatters: LFI allows attackers to read sensitive files from the server OS or execute code via log poisoning.
meta.defaultFix: Use a strict whitelist of allowed file keys rather than passing user input directly to require/include.

findings.name: php version (eol)
findings.detail: PHP version not disclosed in headers

meta.title: PHP Version Disclosure & EOL
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if PHP version is disclosed via X-Powered-By headers and whether that version is end-of-life.
meta.whyItMatters: EOL versions no longer receive security fixes; disclosing the exact version makes targeting known exploits trivial.
meta.defaultFix: Set expose_php = Off in php.ini and upgrade PHP to an actively supported version (8.2+).

meta.title: PHPUnit Eval-Stdin RCE
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed /vendor/phpunit/.../eval-stdin.php test runner endpoint (CVE-2017-9841).
meta.whyItMatters: This endpoint executes arbitrary PHP code sent via POST without authentication.
meta.defaultFix: Remove the /vendor directory from public web access and install test dependencies with --no-dev in production.

meta.title: Python (Django & Flask) Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed requirements.txt, Django debug mode, and Werkzeug/Flask interactive debugger.
meta.whyItMatters: Werkzeug interactive debugger allows unauthenticated remote code execution via interactive console.
meta.defaultFix: Set DEBUG = False in Django and disable debug mode in Flask before deploying to production.

findings.name: rate limiting
findings.detail: 15/15 burst requests succeeded — no rate limiting detected (brute-force risk)
findings.fix: Implement rate limiting at the application level (e.g., Laravel's ThrottleRequests) or web server level (e.g., Nginx 'limit_req') to protect against brute-force and DoS attacks.

meta.title: Rate Limiting & Abuse Prevention
meta.plainExplanation: Tests whether rapid bursts of requests trigger HTTP 429 Too Many Requests or rate-limit headers.
meta.whyItMatters: Endpoints without rate limiting are vulnerable to denial of service, credential stuffing, and scraping.
meta.defaultFix: Implement rate limiting at the reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx limit_req) or application layer.

meta.title: Robots.txt & Sitemap Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Analyzes robots.txt and sitemap.xml for disallow rules pointing to sensitive hidden directories.
meta.whyItMatters: Attackers read robots.txt to discover hidden admin panels, staging areas, and private endpoints.
meta.defaultFix: Do not rely on robots.txt for security; enforce authentication on all sensitive endpoints.

findings.name: security headers
findings.fix: Implement the missing security headers in your web server configuration (e.g., in Nginx 'add_header' or Apache 'Header set') to protect against XSS, clickjacking, and mime-type sniffing.

meta.title: HTTP Security Headers
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for critical defensive headers: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.
meta.whyItMatters: Missing security headers leaves users exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and cross-site scripting.
meta.defaultFix: Configure your web server to supply HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Referrer-Policy headers.

meta.title: Sensitive Files & Configurations
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed database dumps, configuration backups, credentials, and docker-compose files.
meta.whyItMatters: Leaked configuration and database dump files grant instant access to sensitive databases.
meta.defaultFix: Store backups, SQL dumps, and configuration files outside the web root directory.

meta.title: Server Software Disclosure
meta.plainExplanation: Checks if Server header reveals software names and exact version numbers (e.g., Apache/2.4.41).
meta.whyItMatters: Detailed version information allows attackers to look up specific CVE exploits for that exact version.
meta.defaultFix: Set ServerTokens Prod in Apache or server_tokens off in Nginx.

meta.title: Spring Boot Framework Security
meta.plainExplanation: Checks for exposed Spring Boot Actuator endpoints (/actuator, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump) and Whitelabel error pages.
meta.whyItMatters: Exposed Actuator endpoints can leak environment variables, database credentials, and heap dumps containing cleartext passwords.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict Actuator endpoints using Spring Security or set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info.

meta.whyItMatters: Database error messages reveal schema structures and confirm the presence of SQL injection vulnerabilities.
meta.defaultFix: Disable detailed database error output in production and use generic error messages.

meta.whyItMatters: SQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, read, modify, or delete the entire database.
meta.defaultFix: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all database interactions; avoid string concatenation.

meta.whyItMatters: If a third-party CDN is compromised, scripts without SRI hashes can inject malicious code directly into your visitors' browsers.
